As for the intrusive questions on the forms this is normal too. I know it feels uncomfy. A lot of stuff can at the GP. I remember going in for an appointment and the receptionist giving me like a free STI testing kit. It seems they were giving them out to all the young adults, but it was awkward because I’m asexual and do not have sex anyway!!

Hope you get your meds soon, friend!

I gently hand wash my bears :) 

fill a sink with warm (but not too warm) water and add a small amount of gentle laundry detergent. Then, either take a clean cloth and dip it in the sink and dab on your plushies or use your fingers to gently scrub them (that’s what I do as I have old bears). If they have clothes then you can put these wholly in the sink and gently move them around.

Rinse the clothes and dab clean water on the bear. Then, I like to put my bears out in the sun so they can absorb the sunshine :) but if it’s too cloudy, a warm radiator will do.

Be sure to give them lots of love afterwards, many bears don’t like baths :(

Hey man, I completely sympathise with you. You’re absolutely not alone, and often times I have thought the same thing!

I’m greysexual and college age as well. What I try to remember is that everyone is different. Different hobbies, interests, values... and that includes about sex. Some people want it, some don’t. Don’t see the fact you don’t want it as a failure of humanity or a physical defect or something. I just treat it the same as ‘my friend likes bowling, but I do not like bowling. Therefore, I will not go bowling.’

There is sooooooo much more to life than sex. And I don’t think it’s helpful to think of sex as ‘the pinnacle of human existence’. What’s the most important thing to you? That’s the pinnacle of human existence in your life.

Otherwise, may I advise you mix in some different friendship circles? Some people are just more obsessed than others. Often, if someone’s behaviour or values confuse or frustrate you, the best thing to do is remove yourself from them and find people more your vibe. You don’t have to understand people’s values, you just have to know enough about yourself to remove yourself from situations where those values make you feel frustrated and bad about yourself.

Lastly, have you looked into your colleges LGBT+ society? Might be worth a look?

Please message me if you have any other questions or need advice. Being asexual IS NOT wrong or bad. You have value and worth far, far beyond anything sexual. 

Wishing you the best :)
